entry.title: Abdoulkader Waberi Askar (Wikipedia — did you know?)
entry.content: ... that all sporting events in Djibouti were banned for three days after the death of Abdoulkader Waberi Askar?

entry.title: 1925 Tri-State tornado (Wikipedia — did you know?)
entry.content: ... that the 1925 Tri-State tornado was the deadliest in United States history?

entry.title: Annilese Miskimmon (Wikipedia — did you know?)
entry.content: ... that Annilese Miskimmon directed a choose-your-own-ending production of Mozart's Così fan tutte?

entry.title: an academic dishonesty scandal (Wikipedia — did you know?)
entry.content: ... that more than 60 student athletes were involved in an academic dishonesty scandal at Florida State University between 2006 and 2007?

entry.title: Malik Ambersley (Wikipedia — did you know?)
entry.content: ... that Malik Ambersley escaped homelessness by making TikTok Live content in which he pretended to be a non-player character version of the superhero Miles Morales?

entry.title: Polish prisoners of war in World War II (Wikipedia — did you know?)
entry.content: ... that Polish prisoners of war in World War II were held not only by Nazi Germany but also by the Soviet Union?

entry.title: Kerekorio Manu Rangi (Wikipedia — did you know?)
entry.content: ... that the death of child monarch Kerekorio Manu Rangi in 1867 ended the ancient dynasty of Easter Island, which according to local belief "went back to the gods themselves"?

entry.title: violin performance scam (Wikipedia — did you know?)
entry.content: ... that a widespread violin performance scam was described by radio host Scott Simon as "one more raindrop in the storm of schemes that blur our view of what's right in front of us"?
